item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Mixed, leaning negative. There are real pro-equality signals in 2024, especially the appointment of a female prime minister, merit-based education reforms, and some child- and disability-inclusive program design. But the broader record is dominated by repression of activists and journalists, arbitrary detention, and state practices that undermined dignity and equal protection.

**Accepted Claims**
- [DR Congo president appoints country's first female prime minister](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/) | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa, DRC’s first female prime minister. That is a real inclusion signal and directly supports equal-opportunity rather than purely aggregate-welfare governance. | IDs: 6B.8
- [Biographie de la Première Ministre](https://www.primature.gouv.cd/biographie-de-la-premiere-ministre/) | Primature | 2024 | Suminwa’s official biography stresses applied economics, banking, UN/PNUD experience, and development-planning work. That supports a competence-plus-inclusion reading rather than a pure loyalty appointment. | IDs: 6B.8
- [DR Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes) | World Bank | 2024-02-28 | The education project explicitly aimed at students with disabilities, girls’ access, merit-based teacher recruitment, and decentralized planning. This is the clearest evidence I found for protecting equal opportunity through service design, not just aggregate output. | IDs: 6B.8, 6B.2, 6B.5
- [UNICEF cash-transfer gender/social protection report](https://www.unicef.org/innocenti/reports/grassp-democratic-republic-congo) | UNICEF Innocenti | 2024-02 | A cash-transfer program in Kinshasa-area neighborhoods targeted the most vulnerable households and also trained local associations on women’s leadership, women’s rights, and gender-based violence. That is positive evidence for dignity and subgroup-sensitive support. | IDs: 6B.8, 6B.6
- [UNICEF scales up efforts to protect children from mpox outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://www.unicef.org/press-releases/unicef-scales-efforts-protect-children-mpox-outbreak-democratic-republic-congo) | UNICEF | 2024-09-12 | UNICEF’s response plan prioritized children under 15 in 12 provinces and described free treatment for a child. That is a concrete dignity/equal-protection signal for a vulnerable group during a crisis. | IDs: 6B.8, 6B.6
- [DR Congo: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said Tshisekedi had made numerous human-rights pledges but little progress, and that socioeconomic injustice and shrinking civic space persisted. This is strong negative evidence against dignity-centered rule. | IDs: 6B.8
- [DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-30 | Amnesty said the state of siege militarized daily life and that the government failed to protect civilians and address deep-rooted socioeconomic injustices. That cuts directly against a dignity-first reading. | IDs: 6B.8, 6B.7
- [DR Congo: Second term should focus rights](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | HRW said Tshisekedi’s first term ended with repression, arbitrary arrests, and mistrust in democratic institutions, and urged human-rights-centered governance. This is strong evidence that dignity and equal treatment were not being reliably protected. | IDs: 6B.8
- [World Report 2024: Democratic Republic of Congo](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo) | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | HRW reported ongoing repression against journalists, activists, critics, and opposition members, plus police violence against peaceful protest. That is direct counterevidence to dignity and equal-citizenship protection. | IDs: 6B.8, 6B.7
- [DR Congo: Reinstating executions shows a callous disregard for human rights](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/drc-reinstating-executions-shows-a-callous-disregard-for-human-rights/) | Amnesty International | 2024-03-15 | Restoring executions was framed as a hardline response to violence, but Amnesty said it endangered people on death row and violated the right to life. That is strong negative evidence for dignity protection. | IDs: 6B.8, 6B.7
- [Human Rights Agenda for the Democratic Republic of Congo](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/human-rights-agenda-democratic-republic-congo) | Human Rights Watch | 2024-03-06 | HRW noted that elections were marred by irregularities and violence, and that the new term should reverse rights backsliding. This supports the view that equal political dignity was not secure. | IDs: 6B.8, 4B.1

**Search Gap**
- I did not find a 2024 source that directly measured dignity or equal opportunity outcomes across groups in a systematic way.
- The best positive evidence is programmatic and design-level, not proof of broad lived equality.
- The strongest negative evidence is rights- and repression-based, not a dedicated national equality audit.
